newsitem.title: USA: US spot jet fuel prices fall with futures, diffs.
newsitem.headline: US spot jet fuel prices fall with futures, diffs.

text.p: U.S. spot jet fuel prices fell by half a cent to a whole cent a gallon tracking weaker heating oil on the NYMEX as well softer differentials in both Houston and New York Harbor spot markets, traders said.
The reasons for the weaker diffs were distinct in both markets, though both were related to Colonial Pipeline.

USG softness was linked to Colonial's decision to allocate space on its Houston-to-New York distillate line in November, while the weakness in NYG was linked to Colonial forcing jet fuel players to vacate tankage they had making use of at Colonial's Linden, New Jersey terminus, traders said.

The weakness in NYH was focused on low-sulphur 55-grade material, with diffs weakening 0.50 cent to between 1.75 and 2.00 cents over November heating oil futures, which slipped amid views low stocks look likely to be replenished.

In Houston spot markets, prompt airline-quality 54-grade material trade at 2.60 cents under the November print, or about 0.35 cent weaker than on Wednesday due to the Colonial allocation plan which has left some barrels stranded.
The allocation program was also hitting the low sulphur 55-grade in Houston as well, with diffs pegged at between 1.50 cents and 1.00 cent under November futures.
Prompt NYH airline-quality 54-grade material was meanwhile heard done in NYH at 1.20 cents over November NYMEX, with some bids heard at 0.85 cent or about 0.20 cent weaker.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1633
